Title: Diagnosis

Details:
The failing test `testInnerEmptyNamespaceDOM()` calls `doTest("b:foo/test", DocumentContainer.MODEL_DOM, "/b:foo[1]/test[1]")`. The `doTest` method creates a new JXPathContext from a DocumentContainer built from an XML resource and then asserts that the path obtained from the pointer for "b:foo/test" matches the expected path "/b:foo[1]/test[1]`.

The current bug report clarifies that resetting the default namespace to empty (`xmlns=""`) in an XML document leads to an endless loop when `.asPath()` is called on a node. Specifically, the example points to a node `<test xmlns="">` inside a `<b:foo xmlns:b="bla" xmlns="test111">` element, i.e. the default namespace is reset inside the element, resulting in a node with no namespace.

Consulting the test's XML file ("InnerEmptyNamespace.xml", used in `createDocumentContainer`) is important but the report already gives the partial content and the problematic situation involves an inner element with its default namespace reset to empty.

The `doTest` method asserts the `.asPath()` of the pointer to "b:foo/test" is "/b:foo[1]/test[1]", which involves navigating a prefixed element (namespace "b") and then a child element with an empty namespace (because of reset `xmlns=""`). The bug report states that when `.asPath()` is called on such a node, the code enters an endless loop.

From the `JXPathContext.getPointer(String)` methods, the pointer resolves correctly to a `NodePointer` for the xpath "b:foo/test". The issue is thus in the `.asPath()` method of the pointer or related namespace handling code.

The root cause is the handling of XML namespace contexts, especially resetting the default namespace. When default namespace is declared at a higher level and then reset to empty (`xmlns=""`), nodes inside have no namespace. The path generating logic for `.asPath()` seems to mishandle this scenario, probably due to incorrect or infinite recursion when computing the namespace prefix or node name in the case of default namespace resetting.

There is no sign this problem appears in recent related reports. It is isolated to the DOM model and this namespace reset scenario in `.asPath()` path computation.

Summary:
The .asPath() function enters an infinite loop due to improper handling of nodes that reset the default namespace `xmlns=""` inside a prefixed element. The path computation code cycling through ancestors and namespaces does not anticipate or guard against empty default namespaces causing loops. This leads to an endless loop and thus the test fails or hangs.

Next step would be inspecting the `Pointer.asPath()` implementation and related namespace resolution code to identify where the infinite recursion or loop occurs when handling empty default namespaces. Fixing would involve adding guards or correct logic for the empty default namespace handling in `.asPath()` path building.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
